{
  "jobspec": "#!/bin/bash

# Flux batch script
#
# This is a self-submitting Flux script: run it directly (e.g., `./winograd.flux.sh`).
# It will submit itself to Flux with the translated resource requests.

# Translated resources from Slurm:
#   --nodes=1, --ntasks-per-node=1 -> -N 1 -n 1
#   --cpus-per-task=1              -> -c 1
#   --time=4:00:00                 -> -t 4h
#   --gres=gpu:1                   -> -g 1
#   --output=winograd.out          -> -o output=winograd.out
JOBID=$(flux batch -N 1 -n 1 -c 1 -g 1 -t 4h -o output=winograd.out --wrap "bash $0 __flux_inner")

echo "Submitted Flux job: $JOBID"

if [ "${1:-}" = "__flux_inner" ]; then
  # NOTE: Slurm --account=ece_gy_7123-2024sp not translated.
  # Performance/ops implication: accounting/charging may not be applied as intended; some sites require project/account specified out-of-band.

  # NOTE: Slurm --partition=n1s8-v100-1 not translated.
  # Performance implication: without a queue/constraint mapping, the job may run on any eligible GPU resources; you are not forcing the V100 partition.

  # NOTE: Slurm --mem=25GB not translated.
  # Performance implication: without a memory reservation/limit, the job may contend for memory or be OOM-killed, affecting reliability/performance.

  # NOTE: Slurm --job-name=winograd not translated.
  # Performance/ops implication: job identification may be less convenient; runtime performance is unaffected.

  # NOTE: Slurm --mail-type/--mail-user not translated.
  # Performance implication: none; operational implication: no email notifications.

  module purge
  cd /home/pa2497/Thai-Winograd || exit 1

  OVERLAY_FILE=/scratch/pa2497/overlay-25GB-500K.ext3:rw
  SINGULARITY_IMAGE=/scratch/pa2497/cuda11.4.2-cudnn8.2.4-devel-ubuntu20.04.3.sif

  # Run inside the allocation.
  flux run -n 1 -c 1 -g 1 \
    singularity exec --nv \
      --overlay "$OVERLAY_FILE" "$SINGULARITY_IMAGE" \
      /bin/bash -c "source /ext3/env.sh; bash hpc/run_evaluation.sh"
fi
"
}
